title: Pressure ulcers: site, stage and healing
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's pressure ulcer, if any.
note:
Chief Complaint: Pressure ulcer management

Vitals: BP 138/82, HR 76, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 98.4°F, BMI 27.2

Recent Labs: Hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, White Blood Cell Count 7.2 x 10^9/L, Serum Albumin 3.2 g/dL, Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL.

Social History: Retired construction worker. Lives with his wife in a single-story home. Uses a walker for ambulation. Non-smoker.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had a history of stroke.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever or chills.
Integumentary: Positive for skin breakdown at the sacrum.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for decreased mobility.
Neurological: Negative for numbness or tingling.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

HPI: [Copied Forward from previous visit]
Patient is an 84-year-old male presenting for follow-up of a chronic pressure injury. He reports increased difficulty with repositioning and noted that the area has worsened since the last encounter. He denies any new systemic symptoms.

[Today's Update]
The patient presents today for a scheduled evaluation of his sacral wound. He reports that the area remains painful when he is turned in bed. He reports compliance with the current dressing regimen but notes that the wound bed appears to have deeper tissue involvement.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
Integumentary: Physical examination reveals a large pressure ulcer over the sacrum. The wound measures approximately 5cm x 6cm. It is characterized as a stage 4 pressure ulcer with visible exposed tissue. The surrounding skin is intact but shows some maceration. No purulent drainage is noted today.

Assessment:
1. Stage 4 pressure ulcer of the sacrum.

Plan:
1. Continue current wound care protocol.
2. Apply hydrocolloid dressing to the sacrum daily.
3. Instructed patient and caregivers on the importance of frequent repositioning every 2 hours.
4. Scheduled for a follow-up wound measurement in 7 days.
5. Encouraged high-protein nutritional intake to support tissue repair.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Multivitamin daily

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Pressure ulcer of the sacral region, stage 4: L89.154 (HCC 379).

distractors.why: The stage is documented: it decides the code and the HCC.
